title: Relationships: friends forever
subtitle: love at first sight, kindred spirits, thick as thieves
summary: Describe love and friendship with the idioms native speakers really use - hitting it off, getting on like a house on fire, and being as thick as thieves.

lesson.heading: Love and romance
lesson.text: If it is **love at first sight**, love began the first time two people saw each other. To **fall head over heels in love** is to fall deeply and madly in love. If someone **only has eyes for** one person, they are attracted to no one else.

examples.text: When Tom met Lily, it was **love at first sight**.
She fell **head over heels in love** with him.
Nick **only has eyes for** Sophie. He's not interested in other girls.

lesson.heading: Obsessed, or just friends
lesson.text: Someone **infatuated with** another person is romantically obsessed with them; someone **besotted with** them is almost stupidly or blindly in love. A **platonic relationship** is an affectionate relationship between people of the opposite sex that is not sexual.

examples.text: Lauren was more than **infatuated** with Dave; she was completely **besotted** with him.
He's completely **besotted** with her. I've never known him to be so much in love before.
I've often seen Matt and Ellie at the cinema together, but it's purely a **platonic relationship**.

lesson.heading: Friendship idioms
rows: liked each other the moment you met
people who feel close in spirit and understand each other deeply
a man/woman after my own heart
someone you admire because they think or act as you do
get on like a house on fire
have a very good, enjoyable relationship
always want to be together, very close
a relationship or feeling of togetherness

lesson.heading: Friendship in use
lesson.text: These idioms are warm and informal, and they are extremely common in speech. Notice the fixed prepositions: you **hit it off with** someone, you **get on like a house on fire with** them, and there is **a close bond between** two people.

examples.text: Anona and I **hit it off** immediately; we're true **soulmates**.
The moment I met Rob, I could see he was a man **after my own heart**.
Charlie and I **get on like a house on fire**.
Marta and Carmen are **inseparable**, and there's a **close bond** between Rushda and her aunt.

lesson.heading: Collocations for social relationships
rows: you think and look at life the same way
they seem perfect for each other
they're always phoning their brothers and sisters
I know several people she knows
you have a number of **mutual acquaintances**
he has a lot of respect for her

lesson.heading: The prepositions that follow them
lesson.text: Each of these words takes its own preposition, and getting them right is what makes advanced English sound natural: **devoted to**, **respect for**, **loyal to**, **supportive of**, **fond of**, **trust in**, **affectionate towards**, **passionate about**.

examples.text: She's absolutely **devoted to** her mother and visits her every day.
He's very **supportive of** his colleagues; they're very lucky.
I'm quite **fond of** Simon, but that doesn't mean I want to marry him.
Over the years she developed a **fondness for** Mario that went beyond a business relationship.
He was a great team captain who inspired **loyalty** in the players.

lesson.text: A trusting person trusts other people; a trustworthy person can be trusted by other people. They are not the same.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of these expressions.
When Josh met Emma, it was love ___.
exercises.explanation: Love at first sight means love began the first time they saw each other.

exercises.prompt: Phil and Toby look at life in the same way. They're ___.
exercises.explanation: Kindred spirits think and look at life in the same way.

exercises.prompt: Ever since they worked together, Lucy and Olivia have been ___ pals.
exercises.explanation: Bosom friends, buddies or pals are very close, good friends.

exercises.prompt: I was introduced to Zoe by some mutual ___.
exercises.explanation: Mutual acquaintances are people that both of you know.

exercises.prompt: When Ross and I met, we immediately ___.
exercises.hint: (three words: liked each other at once)
exercises.explanation: To hit it off is to like each other the moment you meet.

exercises.prompt: Rachel only has ___ for Mark these days. She's crazy about him.
exercises.explanation: If you only have eyes for someone, you are attracted to no one else.

exercises.prompt: They look such a ___ couple. I wonder if they will get married?
exercises.hint: (one hyphenated word: perfect for each other)
exercises.explanation: A well-matched couple seem perfect for each other.

exercises.prompt: Tara and I have always got on like a house ___.
exercises.explanation: To get on like a house on fire is to have a very good, enjoyable relationship.

exercises.prompt: Matt would do anything for his boss - he holds her in very high ___.
exercises.explanation: To hold someone in high regard is to have a lot of respect for them.

exercises.prompt: I think she was quite right to say what she did - she's a woman after my own ___.
exercises.explanation: A man or woman after your own heart is someone you admire because they think as you do.

exercises.prompt: The children must be planning something - they look as ___ as thieves.
exercises.explanation: People who are as thick as thieves are very close and share all their secrets.

exercises.prompt: They spend most of their holidays in the south of Italy because of their ___ ties there.
exercises.explanation: Family ties are the connections and obligations between relatives.

exercises.prompt: She's absolutely devoted ___ her mother and visits her every day.
exercises.explanation: You are devoted to someone, and loyal to someone.

exercises.prompt: He's very supportive ___ his colleagues; they're very lucky.
exercises.explanation: Supportive of, and fond of, both take of.

exercises.prompt: I feel very affectionate ___ him but I'm not in love with him.
exercises.explanation: You feel affectionate towards someone, though the noun is affection for someone.

exercises.prompt: Sophie and Dan are as passionate ___ each other as they were ten years ago.
exercises.explanation: You are passionate about someone or something.

exercises.prompt: An affectionate relationship between a man and a woman that is not sexual is called ___.
exercises.explanation: A platonic relationship is affectionate but not sexual.

exercises.statement: If someone is trustworthy, it means they trust other people easily.
exercises.explanation: Trustworthy means other people can trust them. Someone who trusts others easily is trusting.

exercises.prompt: Does each expression describe romantic love or friendship?
Put this sentence about a friendship in order.
exercises.answer: Anona and I hit it off immediately; we're true soulmates
exercises.explanation: Soulmates feel close in spirit and understand each other deeply.
